title: Milo the penguin: 30s 3D animated adventure-comedy (Seedance 2.5)
prompt_text: Create an exactly 30-second 3D animated adventure-comedy in 16:9 horizontal format. Use the attached Milo character sheet as the exact visual reference for Milo. Maintain his identical face, brown eyes, three-feather head tuft, charcoal-grey feathers, cream belly, muted golden neck patches, narrow curved dark beak, long thin flippers, tall pear-shaped proportions, oversized pinkish-grey webbed feet and overall silhouette throughout the entire video. The reference defines Milo's appearance only. The story takes place in one continuous sunny autumn forest-edge clearing. An old wild apple tree grows near the upper part of a broad gently sloping grassy hill. One enormous ripe glossy red apple is already lying naturally on the ground beneath the tree before Milo arrives. The apple is approximately the same height as Milo's torso and head combined. It is far too heavy for him to lift but round enough that he can roll it by pushing. Several meters away lies exactly one naturally detached broad curved slab of tree bark. The bark is approximately twice Milo's body length, shallowly concave like a natural tray, thick and rigid enough to keep its shape, and wide enough to support the giant apple with Milo sitting behind it. The bark was already detached before the story begins, and Milo never tears it from a tree. A clear grassy trail leads gently downhill from the apple tree. Near the bottom of the hill is one deep pile of loose dry orange and golden autumn leaves positioned directly across the trail. Immediately beyond and slightly beside that leaf pile is Milo's small round forest shelter entrance built naturally into an earth bank. The entrance is visibly smaller than the giant apple. Keep the apple tree uphill and the shelter downhill for the entire video. Use a premium photorealistic 3D CGI animated feature-film aesthetic with highly detailed soft penguin feathers, realistic bark, glossy apple skin, dry autumn leaves, lush vegetation, expressive character animation, cinematic warm daylight, vibrant natural colors and exaggerated physical-comedy timing. Maintain realistic gravity, friction, momentum, weight, collisions and object support underneath the stylized animation. Use warm sunny autumn daylight throughout with natural cinematic depth of field. There is no dialogue, no text, no subtitles, no logos, no HUD and no additional characters. From 0:00 to 0:02, open with a wide low tracking shot. Milo suddenly bursts through a patch of low autumn plants and runs into the sunny clearing. His oversized webbed feet rapidly slap against the grass, his long flippers swing beside him and his three-feather tuft bounces slightly. Milo suddenly stops when he sees the enormous glossy red apple beneath the old tree. Warm sunlight reflects from its surface. Milo's eyes widen, his beak opens slightly and his expression immediately becomes excited. From 0:02 to 0:04, move into a medium frontal shot beside the apple. Milo inspects the enormous fruit, then crouches beside its lowest accessible side. He slides both long flippers underneath it as far as physically possible, bends his knees and tries to lift. The apple does not move. Milo strains harder while his oversized webbed feet begin slipping slightly backward through the grass, but the apple remains fully supported by the ground. From 0:04 to 0:06, use a wide side shot. Milo makes one final enormous lifting effort. His flippers lose their grip against the smooth apple and he falls backward onto the grass. The apple stays completely stationary. Milo lies dazed for a brief moment, raises his head, looks at the apple and then scans the clearing. His eyes stop on the broad curved piece of detached bark lying nearby. He looks at the bark, then at the apple, then back at the bark. His expression changes as he gets an idea. From 0:06 to 0:08, use a wide side tracking shot that clearly shows Milo's full body, both webbed feet and the entire bark slab at the same time. Milo quickly runs to one narrow end of the bark and remains completely standing on the grass. He does not sit, stand, kneel or ride on the bark. Milo faces the bark, bends forward and grips the narrow end using both long flippers. Both oversized webbed feet stay firmly on the ground. Milo begins walking backward toward the apple, stepping backward with one foot and then the other. His feet press against the grass and provide the traction that moves his body backward. Because both flippers are gripping the bark, his backward movement pulls the bark across the ground toward him. Most of the bark remains continuously supported by and in contact with the grass. The bark never moves underneath Milo and Milo's body never rests on it. He drags it all the way to the giant apple and releases it. From 0:08 to 0:11, use one clear wide side shot showing Milo, the complete apple and the entire bark slab. Milo positions the bark flat on the grass immediately downhill from the apple with its shallow concave surface facing upward. One end lies close to the fruit. Milo walks around to the uphill side of the apple, places both flippers against it and pushes. His webbed feet remain firmly planted on the ground. The apple slowly rotates forward, first one quarter turn and then another, until it rolls directly onto the center of the curved bark slab. Milo immediately stops pushing. The apple settles naturally into the shallow concave center while the bark remains fully supported by the ground. From 0:11 to 0:13.5, show a wide lateral view. Milo walks behind the loaded bark sled and places both long flippers firmly against its rear edge while both feet remain completely on the grass. He leans his pear-shaped body forward and pushes. The bark begins scraping slowly across the nearly flat ground. His feet visibly push backward against the grass with every step. Milo remains on the ground and does not ride the bark yet. The apple remains nested in the center and moves together with the bark as one loaded sled. From 0:13.5 to 0:15.5, use a wide side shot clearly showing the ground transitioning from almost flat grass into a gentle downhill trail. Milo continues pushing from behind. The front half of the loaded bark reaches the downward slope. As more of the sled moves onto the incline, gravity begins pulling it forward. Milo notices that it is becoming easier to push. The bark gradually starts moving slightly faster than Milo's walking pace. Milo removes his flippers from the rear edge and begins running directly behind it. From 0:15.5 to 0:18, use a dynamic side tracking shot. The loaded bark continues sliding downhill at a moderate speed because of gravity. Milo runs behind it using his oversized webbed feet. He catches up while the sled is still moving slowly enough to board safely. Milo reaches forward and places both flippers over the rear side edges of the bark. He takes two quick running steps, places one webbed foot onto the rear portion of the bark, then the second foot, and immediately lowers his body. Milo sits securely behind the giant apple and grips the bark edges with both flippers. This is the first time in the entire video that Milo sits or rides on the bark. From 0:18 to 0:21, use a wide cinematic tracking shot moving alongside the trail. The loaded bark sled continues sliding naturally down the gentle hill. Dry leaves scatter slightly underneath the front and side edges. The trail remains completely clear. The bark stays continuously in contact with the ground. The apple remains seated securely in the shallow concave center and does not roll independently. Milo sits directly behind it. At first he looks nervous and grips the bark tightly. After a moment, he realizes the ride is stable. His expression slowly changes from concern to excitement and a delighted smile appears. From 0:21 to 0:23.5, move into a closer side tracking shot. The downhill trail becomes slightly steeper but remains smooth and safe, causing gravity to moderately increase the sled's speed. Milo continues gripping the bark edges. His charcoal-grey feathers and three-feather tuft move gently in the rushing air. He looks forward and realizes everything appears under control. His confidence grows. Milo straightens his upper body slightly while remaining securely seated, pushes his chest forward and smiles proudly as though the entire ride was planned. From 0:23.5 to 0:25.5, use a front-facing tracking shot moving backward downhill. Milo continues riding proudly behind the giant apple. He looks past the fruit toward the bottom of the hill. Camera pulls slightly wider and reveals the enormous deep pile of orange and golden autumn leaves directly across the trail. Beyond and slightly beside the pile is Milo's small shelter entrance. Milo initially smiles when he sees home, but then notices how quickly the leaf pile is approaching. His expression changes immediately and he grips both sides of the bark more tightly. From 0:25.5 to 0:27, use one uninterrupted wide side-profile shot. The loaded bark sled enters the deep pile of loose dry autumn leaves. The leaves create strong resistance and friction against the bark, causing the sled to rapidly but smoothly lose speed. A large soft burst of orange and golden leaves sprays outward. The bark remains flat against the ground and never flips. The giant apple stays inside the shallow center and does not launch forward. Milo naturally leans forward because of the deceleration but remains seated safely behind the apple. The sled comes to a complete stop inside the soft leaf pile. Nothing breaks. From 0:27 to 0:28.5, use a medium shot beside the leaf pile. Milo climbs carefully off the stopped bark sled and steps onto the grass. He looks at the giant apple, then turns toward his nearby shelter entrance. His proud smile returns. Milo positions himself behind the apple, places both flippers against it and pushes. The apple rolls slowly off the bark with one controlled rotation and then another. Milo continues walking behind it and pushing it across the short flat patch of ground toward the shelter. From 0:28.5 to 0:30, finish with a static frontal comedy shot facing the shelter entrance. The enormous red apple rolls directly toward the small round doorway. Its diameter is clearly larger than the opening. The curved sides of the apple contact the earth around both sides of the entrance and it stops with a low soft thud. Milo continues pushing for one brief moment but nothing moves. He stops, looks at the shelter entrance, looks at the enormous apple, looks back at the entrance, then slowly looks at the apple again. After one small silent beat, Milo calmly walks around the side of the fruit, sits comfortably on the grass, leans toward the apple and takes one enormous satisfied bite. His eyes close happily and he smiles. Cut to black. Maintain strict Milo consistency throughout all 30 seconds. Never alter his facial structure, brown eyes, three-feather tuft, charcoal-grey feathers, cream belly, muted golden neck patches, dark curved beak, long thin flippers, oversized pinkish-grey webbed feet, pear-shaped body or overall silhouette. There is exactly one giant red apple. It begins resting on the ground beneath the apple tree and remains the exact same fruit throughout the entire video. It never falls from the tree, teleports, duplicates or changes size. There is exactly one curved bark slab. It begins lying naturally on the grass and Milo physically moves it. The bark never moves by itself before Milo pushes it onto the visible downhill slope. It never floats, flies, flips, changes size, changes shape or behaves like fabric. Before 0:15.5, Milo must never sit, stand, kneel, balance or ride on the bark. During the 0:06 to 0:08 dragging action, Milo remains entirely on the grass. Both webbed feet must remain clearly visible on the ground while he walks backward and pulls the bark using both flippers. Never depict Milo sitting on the same bark that he is trying to drag. During the apple-loading and pushing sequence, Milo also remains entirely on the ground. Milo boards the bark for the first time only from 0:15.5 onward after gravity has already started moving the loaded sled downhill. When the apple is on the bark, its full weight remains physically supported by the concave bark surface. The apple never hovers or balances on invisible support. During the downhill ride, the apple stays in direct contact with the bark and does not independently roll ahead or backward. The loaded sled moves slowly across flat ground only while Milo physically pushes it. Continued motion and acceleration occur only once the sled reaches the visible downhill slope and gravity acts on it. The leaf pile is already present before Milo reaches it and contains only loose dry leaves. There are no hidden rocks, logs or hard objects inside. The increasing friction and resistance of the leaves gradually stop the sled. Milo does not fly out, the bark does not flip and the apple does not launch forward. The shelter entrance remains exactly the same size throughout the video and the apple remains exactly the same size. The ending works only because the apple was already wider than the doorway. The doorway never shrinks and the apple never grows. Maintain one continuous uphill-to-downhill geography. The apple tree remains uphill and the shelter remains downhill. Do not mirror or reverse the environment between shots. Once Milo passes a location, it remains geographically behind him. No teleportation, object duplication, object regeneration, invisible supports, spontaneous acceleration, unexplained movement, additional animals or humans. Use readable cinematic framing throughout. Use wide lateral views whenever physical cause and effect matters. During the bark-dragging sequence, keep Milo's full body, both webbed feet and the entire bark visible at the same time. During the apple-loading action, clearly show the apple physically rolling onto the bark. During the loaded-sled push, clearly show Milo behind the bark with both feet on the ground. Clearly reveal the terrain becoming downhill before the sled begins moving independently. During boarding, show Milo running behind the sled and physically stepping onto it without hiding the transition. Keep the downhill direction consistent and never use camera rotation to fake sled movement. Use a playful adventurous orchestral score throughout. Include rapid webbed-foot footsteps during Milo's opening run, natural autumn forest ambience, soft wind through leaves, comedic effort sounds while he tries lifting the apple, a soft thump when he falls backward, realistic bark scraping over grass as he drags it, clear webbed footsteps during the dragging action, a low rolling sound as the apple moves onto the bark, heavier scraping as he pushes the loaded sled and gradually more adventurous music when the sled reaches the slope. Add rhythmic dry-leaf and bark-sliding sounds during the downhill ride, light wind rush as the speed increases and a triumphant musical feeling as Milo becomes confident. When the leaf pile appears, shift briefly into playful tension. Use a large soft rush and poof as the sled enters the leaves, followed by falling and settling leaf sounds. Add soft apple-rolling sounds near the shelter, a low thud when the apple contacts the doorway, a tiny pushing effort sound, then brief silence as Milo realizes the problem. Finish with one crisp apple bite and one tiny satisfied orchestral note before cutting to black.

title: Pip the baby dragon in a medieval kitchen (Seedance 2.5)
prompt_text:
🎬 Long Cinematic AI Video Prompt

Prompt

A cozy, lighthearted comedic-cinematic scene set inside a warm, dimly lit rustic medieval cottage kitchen at night, continuing the established dark-fantasy dragon saga's visual world but shifting into a charming domestic comedy tone. Warm amber firelight dominates the palette, soft shadows from a crackling hearth, photorealistic non-cartoonish creature texture work, shallow depth of field, intimate handheld camera, 16:9 widescreen, 24fps cinematic film grain.

**Scene 1 (0–8s):** Close-up on a small pink baby dragon — soft coral-pink frilled spikes running from its head down its spine, pale cream skin dappled with pink spots, delicate translucent wing membranes folded at its sides, and huge round amber eyes — sitting hunched on worn wooden floorboards beside an empty wooden bowl. It stares upward with an exaggerated, heartbreakingly pitiful "starving" expression, eyes wide and glassy, as if it truly hasn't eaten in days, despite its visibly plump little body suggesting otherwise. A black cast-iron cauldron bubbles warmly in the foreground, filled with chunky meat-and-carrot stew, steam curling upward in the firelight.

**Scene 2 (8–16s):** A woman in simple medieval dress — a cream linen blouse with rolled sleeves under a brown wool pinafore — kneels by the hearth, wooden ladle in hand, scooping a generous portion of stew from the cauldron into the dragon's bowl. She glances down at it with a knowing, amused half-smile, clearly familiar with this routine. The dragon's eyes track the ladle hungrily, body practically vibrating with anticipation.

**Scene 3 (16–24s):** The dragon dives into the bowl eagerly, snout buried in the stew, eating with sloppy enthusiasm — chunks of carrot and meat sauce smearing messily across its snout, cheeks, and whiskers. Close-up shots capture its blissful chewing expression, small claws gripping the edge of the bowl possessively. The woman watches, chuckling, shaking her head affectionately at the mess being made.

**Scene 4 (24–32s):** Time compresses through quick, playful cuts — the bowl refilled a second time, then a third, the dragon's belly visibly growing rounder and more swollen with each helping, its movements slowing from eager gulping to sluggish, satisfied nibbling. The woman kneels beside it between refills, one eyebrow raised, pointing a finger at the dragon in gentle, teasing scolding — the universal "you've had enough" gesture — while stew sauce continues to drip down its chin.

**Scene 5 (32–40s):** The dragon, now thoroughly stuffed, flops backward onto the wooden floor, completely overwhelmed by its own gluttony. Its belly is comically round and taut, short stubby legs splayed limply in the air, wings sprawled flat against the floorboards, head tilted to one side with a dazed, deeply satisfied half-smile, a faint smear of stew still on its snout. It looks utterly helpless and adorable in its food-coma state.

**Scene 6 (40–46s):** The woman kneels down beside the fallen dragon, gently resting her palm on its swollen belly and rubbing it slowly and affectionately, laughing softly under her breath at the ridiculous scene. The cauldron continues to simmer gently in the background, the wooden cottage interior glowing warm and lived-in around them — exposed beams, a sturdy wooden table, hanging pots, and flickering hearth light completing the cozy domestic atmosphere.

**Overall tone and theme:** A warm, funny, feel-good interlude within the larger dragon saga — pure comedic relief built on the classic "puppy-dog eyes versus visibly full belly" gag, celebrating the playful, trusting, deeply affectionate bond between the woman and her dragon companion "Pip." Visual continuity maintained with prior installments: same practical-effect creature rendering style (soft wet-look skin, fine scale/frill texture, anatomically grounded but expressive proportions), same rustic medieval-fantasy production design, warm interior firelight as the dominant mood-setter. Sound design implied: crackling fire, contented dragon grunts and satisfied belly-groans, the woman's warm laughter, the clink of the ladle against the cauldron. Aspect ratio 16:9, cinematic film grain, heartwarming and comedic pacing throughout.

title: Anime Bruce Lee vs Mr. Miyagi koi-pond fight (Seedance 2.5)
prompt_text: Cinematic anime clip, 20 seconds. Japanese garden at golden sunset: a koi pond with lily pads, a curved wooden bridge with railings, bonsai trees, a wooden deck along the water’s edge, a tall wooden post rising out of the pond, and orange sunlight glittering on the water. One continuous location. CHARACTER ONE — OLD MAN IN KHAKI SHIRT: Use uploaded character sheet. Calm, light on his feet, faint smile, never breaks a sweat. CHARACTER TWO — MAN IN YELLOW JUMPSUIT WITH NUNCHAKU: Use uploaded character sheet. Explosive, lightning fast, screaming battle cries, relentless. 0:00–0:04 — Already mid-fight from frame one. Tracking two-shot: the man in the yellow jumpsuit attacks with spinning nunchaku while the old man dodges and weaves backward along the wooden deck. Low angle: the nunchaku swings low and the old man hops over it. Side-on two-shot: the old man strikes the man’s wrist with a sharp palm and the nunchaku flies into the pond. Medium two-shot: without stopping, the man in the yellow jumpsuit flows straight into kicks. 0:04–0:08 — Over-the-shoulder shot: a nonstop kick flurry, the man in the yellow jumpsuit screaming with each kick. Medium two-shot: the old man deflects every kick with big circular sweeping arm blocks, both hands moving in wide circles, as he’s pushed back onto the wooden bridge. Side-on two-shot on the bridge: the old man counters with a quick strike to the chest. Low angle: the man in the yellow jumpsuit flips backward off the bridge railing and comes straight back with a flying knee. 0:08–0:12 — Close two-shot: the old man slips the knee and they trade rapid blows in the middle of the bridge. Wide shot: the old man sweeps his legs. Tracking shot: the man in the yellow jumpsuit spins up off the ground into a spinning back kick, the old man ducks, and the kick splinters the bridge railing. 0:12–0:16 — Wide two-shot: still trading strikes, they drive each other off the bridge onto the deck. Medium shot: the man in the yellow jumpsuit lands a hit that sends the old man skidding to the edge of the deck. Low angle: the old man springs off the edge onto the tall wooden post in the pond and lands in the crane stance against the blazing sunset, one leg raised, arms spread wide like wings. 0:16–0:19 — Wide two-shot: the man in the yellow jumpsuit screams and launches a flying kick straight at the post. Side-on two-shot: the old man’s crane kick meets him mid-air. Wide shot: the man in the yellow jumpsuit crashes into the koi pond with a huge splash. 0:19–0:20 — Medium shot: the old man bows from the top of the post. The man in the yellow jumpsuit surfaces with a lily pad on his head and bows back. Cel-shaded 3D anime, Unreal Engine quality, Japanese garden at golden sunset throughout: koi pond, lily pads, wooden bridge, bonsai trees, wooden deck, wooden post in the pond, glittering orange water. Bold flat color blocking, hard edge shadows, thick black outlines, vibrant saturated colors, film grain. Punchy impact sound on every hit. NO slow motion anywhere in the video; everything is full speed, high energy, and continuous. The fight never pauses; every move flows directly into the next. Quick cuts with a new camera angle every shot: tracking two-shots, side-on, over-the-shoulder, low angles, wides, close two-shots. Never static, never the same angle twice, and each action completes before the next cut. Both characters share the frame during every exchange. Same garden throughout, no teleporting. Both characters always match their uploaded character sheets. Chronological beat order always maintained.

title: Bus transforms into a mechanical caterpillar (Seedance 2.5)
prompt_text: An old, green, oversized, and extremely tall American-style bus is parked in a rundown parking lot in the middle of a forest. A young Asian driver slams on the brakes, visibly panicked and speechless. The bus begins to violently disassemble and reassemble itself from the inside out, transforming into a bad-tempered, menacing Cybertronian mechanical giant caterpillar. The cab restructures into a mechanical head, the windshield becomes its eyes/glasses, and the bumper forms its jaw. The sides of its mouth are powered by hydraulic systems, the tongue is constructed from seats, and the teeth are formed by the bus’s broken orange interior handrails. The headlights become its eyes, and the entire body is segmented from large vehicle components. It spits the driver out from its mouth, bites down on his head, then launches him into the air — letting him land on its back, where he grabs the handrails and steadies himself. The mechanical giant caterpillar strikes a cool pose, roars, and shoots out sparks. The windows and tires remain intact throughout. The transformation is aggressive — the body twists and writhes continuously, parts grind and spark, dust billows, and valves release bursts of steam. The camera moves seamlessly from the cab to the exterior, showcasing the mechanical body’s massive yet slender form. The generated material uses a realistic visual style, with a humorous yet horrifying transformation aesthetic.

title: Squirrel vs crocodile river: 20s, 20 beats (Seedance 2.5)
prompt_text: SCENE CONTEXT A red squirrel knocks a giant acorn out of a tree into a crocodile river, dives after it, and fights through snapping jaws to carry it to shore. 20s, 20 beats. ACTIVE REFERENCES @NUTTY - stylised animated red squirrel, ginger-orange fur with a cream face, muzzle and belly, a dark reddish stripe from between the eyes back over the head and down the spine, large round eyes with white sclera and olive-green irises, pink triangular nose, two prominent white buck teeth, small ginger-tufted ears, long white whiskers, enormous bushy ginger tail bigger than his body. 100% matches the reference. @ACORN - giant acorn the size of @NUTTY's torso, smooth mid-brown nut, textured tan cap with a dense diamond scale pattern, short dark stem. 100% matches the reference. @CROC - cartoon river crocodile, olive-sage back, pale yellow-green belly, bumpy ridged spine, long flat snout, big white triangular teeth, amber eyes with slit pupils set high on the skull. Dozens fill the river. 100% matches the reference. @RIVERWOOD - sunlit broadleaf forest, tall pale trunks, green and golden-yellow blossom canopy, dappled forest floor, wide teal-green river, reed banks, sandy pebbled shore. STYLE REFERENCE ONLY, not a fixed keyframe; model extends the world freely, never reproduced 1:1. FIRST FRAME / BLOCKING Non-empty opening frame: @NUTTY is already high on a branch with both arms around @ACORN, already straining, the branch already bending, leaves already shaking loose, tail already counterbalancing. Camera already tilted up the trunk. Nothing is frozen. FORMAT MODE Timed multishot, NINETEEN HARD CUTS at 2.0 2.4 2.8 3.8 4.9 5.3 8.2 8.8 9.4 10.3 11.0 11.8 13.2 13.8 15.4 16.0 17.6 18.4 19.3 seconds. Cuts only at these points, the camera does not cut on its own. ACTION 0.0-2.0 - 63 deg low angle steeply up the trunk, handheld 4cm tremor. @NUTTY wrenches @ACORN free, it tears loose and drops past camera, he lunges and misses. 2.0-2.4 - 29 deg close-up, 4 deg tilt. His head whips down, mouth stretching wide in a scream, ears flattening back. 2.4-2.8 - 18 deg extreme close-up on his eyes only, eyes filling frame. Pupils shrink to dots, whites go wide. 2.8-3.8 - 47 deg falling beside @ACORN, SLOW MOTION. It tumbles end over end, forest streaking to vertical green blur. 3.8-4.9 - 84 deg straight down. @ACORN splashes into the river, ringed by a radial starburst of @CROC jaws gaping open like spokes, then bobs back up among them. 4.9-5.3 - 29 deg close-up on his hind paws gripping bark. He coils, tail stiffening, then springs out of frame. 5.3-8.2 - 47 deg lateral tracking at 50 km/h. @NUTTY glides spread-eagle, body flat and horizontal, tail streaming, pale trunks whipping past in heavy directional blur, face locked in terror. 8.2-8.8 - 12 deg tele head-on. He glides straight down the lens, growing fast, arms spread, the forest compressed flat behind him. 8.8-9.4 - 107 deg super-wide at water level. He punches in nose first, bubbles and foam tearing behind. 9.4-10.3 - 84 deg underwater looking up. @CROC bellies, legs and tails in dark silhouette across the surface, green light shafting between them. 10.3-11.0 - 18 deg underwater extreme close-up. A @CROC jaw yawns open straight at camera. @NUTTY plants both feet on its snout and rockets upward. 11.0-11.8 - 63 deg at the surface. He bursts out in a crown of spray and snatches @ACORN out of the air. 11.8-13.2 - 47 deg lateral tracking at 55 km/h. He sprints across the water on his hind feet, a @CROC lunging in from frame left and missing by a whisker. 13.2-13.8 - 29 deg close-up. Jaws CLAMP shut on his tail tip. He yanks it free, fur puffing out in a cloud. 13.8-15.4 - 84 deg low wide. A @CROC launches its whole body clear of the river. @NUTTY ducks flat and skids under the closing jaws, spray sheeting over him. 15.4-16.0 - 18 deg extreme close-up on his face, SLOW MOTION. Teeth gritted, eyes blazing, water beading off his whiskers, @ACORN hugged to his chest. 16.0-17.6 - 47 deg lateral tracking. He runs the ridged backs of @CROC like stepping stones toward shore, each one bucking and twisting under his feet. 17.6-18.4 - 107 deg super-wide. The last @CROC lunges. He leaps. The jaws close on nothing behind him. 18.4-19.3 - 63 deg. He hits the sandy shore and tumbles over twice, @ACORN rolling with him. 19.3-20.0 - 18 deg extreme close-up. He hugs @ACORN to his chest, chest heaving, eyes half-closed in exhausted relief, one ear twitching. PERFORMANCE @NUTTY plays pure panic with total commitment - ears pinned, eyes enormous, limbs windmilling, every beat a full overreaction. He is never brave, only desperate, and his face resets to terror the instant each escape lands. Relief only arrives in the final frame. The @CROC crocodiles play slow and dumb against his speed: they blink late, snap late, clack shut on empty air and bonk into each other. Stylised animated performance with real weight, clean readable poses, strong silhouettes, a micro-pause before every big reaction. PHYSICS Mass and inertia carry through every fall, glide, splash, bite and leap. @ACORN tumbles with real weight and throws a heavy splash. Water sheets off fur, spray arcs behind the sprint, bubbles rise at proper speed, reeds bend in the wake, crocodile backs sink under his weight. Nothing floats. His big tail trails half a beat behind every direction change and whips when he turns. Correct contact shadows on branch, water, scales and sand. LIGHTING Warm late-morning sun from the upper left through the canopy, visible god-rays and dappled pools on the forest floor, bright bounce off the river filling all shadows so nothing falls dark. Underwater the light turns deep green and falls in shafts from the surface. The final shore beat is lit warm and low with long soft shadows across the sand. Faint haze through the far trees. WB locked 5400K. COLOR GRADE Ginger fur glowing warm against teal-green water, the brown acorn the single solid mass in every frame it appears in, olive crocodiles blending into the reed banks, golden-yellow blossom canopy backlit by the sun, pale trunks catching rim light, white spray against dark water. Rich and saturated, no deep shadow anywhere, color tied to source and surface, not a flat list. AUDIO Full orchestral chase score with fast strings, woodwind runs and heavy comedy percussion, mixed loud. A rising violin scramble under the branch struggle, a sharp stinger as the acorn tears loose, near-silence across the slow-motion fall with only rushing wind, a huge timpani and cymbal hit on the splash, then the score racing flat out through the glide and the water run with a woodwind sting on every jaw snap and a cymbal choke on the tail bite. A warm resolving chord over the shore.

title: Claude + Blender MCP + Remotion: one-evening animation studio
6-file Harness: idea to video with Claude + Remotion (no video model)
prompt_text:
This is my exact prompt that I give to Claude Opus 5.5 to turn an idea into a video; without any video generation model, just with 6 files. Most people tell Claude "make a video" and hope for a good result. But instead of a simple prompt, I give it a Harness; a specific process that it has to execute step by step and create the 6 files in order.
1. First, it analyzes the reference sample. Rhythm, first movement, cut timing, and the moment when the main message peaks. spec.md
2. Then, it checks the accuracy of the numbers. Every number must have its source and related search phrase. If no source is found, it stops and asks a question. data.json
3. Before creating the motion, it writes the story. One main message, one key number, and three stages: hook, proof, and result. story.md
4. It creates each frame with code. Using Remotion and a custom motion design Skill; all displayed values are also variables. Scene.tsx
5. It understands revisions in plain language. For example, you say "the title appears a bit late" and it applies the necessary change; without rebuilding everything from scratch. timing.ts
6. It renders the frames, compares them to the reference sample, and waits before my final approval. final.mp4
A regular prompt gives you one shot; a Harness gives you a process that you can review, revise, and control step by step.

title: Cooking eggs with a curious white dragon: 30s medieval fantasy (Seedance 2.5)
prompt_text:
Create a 30-second ultra-realistic cinematic fantasy scene: a young blonde woman in a white dress cooking eggs in a medieval stone kitchen while a curious white dragon watches from above.

SCENE 1 (0-5s): Wide establishing shot. A medieval stone kitchen with warm candlelight. A young blonde woman in a white medieval dress stands at a rustic hearth, stirring a pan. Cinematic depth of field.

SCENE 2 (5-10s): Camera tilts up to reveal a curious white dragon with large expressive eyes perched on the wooden beams above. The dragon leans down, watching her cook.

SCENE 3 (10-15s): Close-up of the woman's face as she notices the dragon. She smiles warmly and offers it a peek at the cooking eggs with a playful expression.

SCENE 4 (15-20s): Over-the-shoulder shot from behind the woman showing the dragon reaching down with one claw to gently touch the edge of the pan. Warm golden light from the hearth.

SCENE 5 (20-25s): Close-up of the dragon's eye reflecting the fire and the cooking eggs. Magical atmosphere with subtle sparkles in the air.

SCENE 6 (25-30s): Final wide shot. The woman laughing softly as the dragon pulls back, both sharing a quiet magical moment.

VISUAL STYLE: Ultra-realistic 3D cinematic with fantasy realism. Warm color palette dominated by golden candlelight and hearth fire tones. Soft volumetric light rays through steam.

CAMERA: Smooth cinematic camera work. Starts with a slow wide establishing shot, moves into intimate close-ups, uses gentle tilts and over-the-shoulder compositions. Shot on virtual 50mm lens with shallow depth of field.

AUDIO: Warm hearth crackling sounds, subtle egg sizzling, gentle ambient medieval kitchen atmosphere, soft dragon breath sounds, no music - just diegetic sound design.

FORMAT: 16:9 aspect ratio, 30 seconds, 24fps, cinematic color grading with warm fantasy tones.

title: AI video prompt template with continuity rules and restrictions
prompt_text:
Act as a professional film director and AI video prompt engineer. I need you to help me write a detailed, production-ready AI video prompt.

Here's my idea:
IDEA: [Describe your scene in 1-2 sentences]
PURPOSE: [What emotion should the audience feel?]
MAIN CHARACTER: [Appearance, clothing, personality]
ENVIRONMENT: [Setting details, time period, lighting]

Now expand it into a production-ready prompt including:
• ACTION & MOVEMENT: Exactly what happens, the sequence of events, character acting, pacing, and timing
• CAMERA DIRECTION: Shot types (wide, close-up, over-the-shoulder, Dutch angle), camera movement (static, dolly, pan, tracking), lens choice (35mm, 50mm, 85mm), and camera angle (low, eye-level, high, bird's eye)
• LIGHTING & ATMOSPHERE: Quality of light (warm, cold, soft, harsh, directional), light sources, time of day, atmospheric effects (fog, rain, dust, lens flare)
• VISUAL STYLE: Cinematic style, color palette, contrast, film texture. Must specify a consistent look (e.g., 'Photorealistic live-action, desaturated, high contrast, grainy film stock'). Never leave the style ambiguous.

CRITICAL CONTINUITY RULES — add these to your prompt:
• CHARACTER CONSISTENCY: The main character's appearance (hair, clothing, build, face) must be identical in every shot. Lock one reference description and reuse it verbatim in each scene.
• ENVIRONMENT LOCK: Walls, floor, furniture, props, and background must not change between shots unless it's an intentional story reason.
• LIGHTING MATCH: If the scene is lit by sunset in one shot, it must be lit by sunset in the next. Time of day must not jump without a transition.
• PHYSICS & MOTION: Real-world physics. Objects don't float unless supernatural. Movements should flow smoothly without snapping or teleporting.

RESTRICTIONS — enforce these:
• No text, subtitles, logos, watermarks, or UI overlays.
• No morphing, no extra limbs, no warped faces.
• No cartoon/anime look unless that's the explicit style.
• No sudden zooms, shakes, or speed ramps unless I ask for them.

Output only the final copy-ready prompt, nothing else.

title: Treat video like code: frame-exact Claude + Remotion workflow
prompt_text:
npx skills add remotion-dev/skills

Workflow: 1) Fix duration and frame rate (20s at 30fps = 600 frames). 2) Define main events: element entry, motion, result, pause for reading, end. 3) Give Claude exact frame timing per event (button appears by frame 90, click at frame 195, result readable from frame 234). 4) Install the official Remotion skills. 5) Review static key frames before the full render. Flow: Brief, animation generation, static frame review, precise fixes, final render.
